question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

To frighten or threaten someone, usually in order to persuade the person to do something he or she does not wish to do
solution:
The correct answer is: **Intimidate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Intimidate"** means to frighten or threaten someone, usually in order to persuade the person to do something he or she does not wish to do. (धमकाना)

 
 
• **Example:** The bully tried to **intimidate **the smaller kids into giving him their lunch money.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Forceless** (निर्बल): Lacking strength or power.

 
 
• **Example:** His argument was **forceless **and did not convince anyone.
 
 
 
• **Compel** (मजबूर करना): To force or oblige someone to do something.
 
 
• **Example:** The circumstances **compelled **her to take a job she didn’t like.
 
 
 
• **Authoritative** (प्रभावी): Commanding and self-confident; likely to be respected and obeyed.
 
 
• **Example:** His **authoritative **tone convinced everyone to follow his lead.
